questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi called a halt to the Non-Cooperation Movement after the Chauri Chaura incident. Where among the following places is Chauri Chaura located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gorakhpur.
Chauri Chaura, a town in Uttar Pradesh, was the site of a violent clash on February 4, 1922, during the Non-Cooperation Movement. Protesters set a police station on fire, resulting in the deaths of 22 policemen inside. The town is located in the Gorakhpur district.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 resulted in the abolishment of the Tinkathia System.
Reason (R): The Tinkathia System forced peasants to cultivate wheat on 3/20th of their landholdings for British planters.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.
  • Assertion (A) is true: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 resulted in the abolishment of the Tinkathia System.
  • Reason (R) is false: The Tinkathia System forced peasants to cultivate indigo (not wheat) on 3/20th of their landholdings for British planters.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Non-Cooperation Movement launched in 1920 included boycott of foreign goods, promotion of spinning wheels, and picketing at liquor shops.
2. The resolution of Poorna Swaraj was passed at the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in 1920 as part of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920) included boycott of foreign goods, promotion of spinning wheels (charkha), and picketing at liquor shops.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The resolution for Poorna Swaraj was passed at the Lahore session of 1929 (not 1920), under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question: Gandhi gave his slogan of 'Do or Die' during which of the following Movements/Satyagrahas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Quit India.
The Quit India Movement (also known as the August Movement) was launched by the Indian National Congress on August 8, 1942. Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) during this movement.

questions.question: Vallabhbhai Patel and ______ helped Gandhi in Kheda by organising his tour of the villages and urging the peasants to stand firm against the government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indulal Yajnik.
During the Kheda Satyagraha, Indulal Yajnik along with Vallabhbhai Patel helped Gandhi by organizing his tour of the villages and urging the peasants to stand firm against the government. Mahatma Gandhi returned to India on 9 January 1915.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mahatma Gandhi returned his Kaisar-i-Hind medal in 1920 as a protest against the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
2. Rabindranath Tagore returned his Kaisar-i-Hind medal in protest against the same massacre.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.
  • Kaiser-e-Hind title was given to Mahatma Gandhi by Governor-General Lord Hardinge in 1915 for his services during the Boer War (1899-1902). Gandhi returned his title in response to the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (13th April 1919).
  • Rabindranath Tagore returned his Knighthood title (not Kaisar-i-Hind medal) in response to the massacre.

questions.question: In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi successfully led a strike of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mill workers.
The Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) is considered the first hunger strike led by Gandhi. He successfully led a strike of mill workers in Ahmedabad, demanding better wages.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918:
1. The Kheda Satyagraha was launched against the British demand for high land revenue despite crop failure and plague outbreak.
2. The movement was organised mainly by the Patidar peasants of Gujarat under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.
The Kheda Satyagraha of 1918 was a movement in the Kheda district of Gujarat organized by Mahatma Gandhi.
  • It was launched against the British demand for high land revenue despite a devastating crop failure and plague outbreak.
  • The movement was organized mainly by the Patidar peasants of Gujarat.

questions.question: When did depressed classes get the reserved seats in provincial and central legislative councils, but they were to be voted in by the General electorate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is September 1932.
The Poona Pact was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar in September 1932. Under this pact:
  • Seats reserved for the depressed classes were increased from 71 to 147 in provincial legislatures
  • 18 percent of the total seats in the Central Legislature were reserved
  • They were to be voted in by the General electorate

questions.question: Gandhi, aged ______, arrived in India in 1915 from South Africa.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 46.
Gandhi was born on 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat. He went to South Africa in 1893 as a lawyer. He returned to India on 9th January 1915 at the age of 46.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The quote 'Be the change you wish to see in the world' is attributed to Mahatma Gandhi.
2. The quote 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom' was also said by Gandhi.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is True
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.
  • Statement 1 is true: 'Be the change you wish to see in the world' is attributed to Mahatma Gandhi.
  • Statement 2 is false: 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom' was said by Subhas Chandra Bose, not Gandhi.
Other famous Gandhi quotes: 'A man is but the product of his thoughts. What he thinks, he becomes.', 'Nobody can hurt me without my permission.'

questions.question: In which of the following years, did Subhas Chandra Bose refer to Mahatma Gandhi as the 'Father of the Nation'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1944.
Subhas Chandra Bose called Mahatma Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation' in a radio address from Singapore on 6 July 1944.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Khilafat Movement:
1. The All-India Khilafat Conference of November 1919 was held at Delhi.
2. Leaders like the Ali brothers, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Ajmal Khan, and Hasrat Mohani played a key role in this movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.
  • Statement 1 is correct: The All-India Khilafat Conference of November 1919 was held at Delhi.
  • Statement 2 is correct: The movement was led by the Ali brothers (Maulana Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali), Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Ajmal Khan, and Hasrat Mohani.

questions.question: Who among the following called Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose a patriot of patriots?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.
Mahatma Gandhi called Subhash Chandra Bose a 'patriot of patriots'. Rabindranath Tagore called him 'Desh Nayak'. His famous slogans: 'Dilli Chalo', 'Jai Hind', 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom'. His autobiography: 'The Indian Struggle'.

questions.question: Which of the following events occurred as an after-effect of the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (13th April 1919)?
questions.option_1: Hunger strike to settle disputes between the mill owners and the workers
questions.option_2: Individual princes could sign a separate agreement with the British
questions.option_3: Hunter Commission was appointed by the British Government
questions.option_4: Popularisation of Charkha and Khadi and Jail Bharey Congress volunteers
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hunter Commission was appointed by the British Government.
The Hunter Commission came to India in 1919 under the leadership of William Hunter to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. (Note: Another Hunter Commission on Indian Education was prepared in 1882 by William Wilson Hunter.)

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for slowing down the Non-cooperation Movement?
questions.option_1: Due to the absence of alternative Indian institution, boycott of British Institutions posed a problem.
questions.option_2: Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void.
questions.option_3: Many lawyers resigned but then absence of income for a longer period of time compelled them to rejoin.
questions.option_4: Khadi cloth was often more expensive than mass-produced mill cloth and poor people could not afford to buy it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void.
This statement is not a valid reason for slowing down the Non-cooperation Movement. The actual reasons included:
  • Lack of alternative Indian institutions made boycotting British institutions difficult
  • Many lawyers who resigned eventually rejoined due to lack of income
  • Khadi was more expensive than mill cloth, making it unaffordable for the poor

questions.question: In which of the following years was the civil disobedience campaign completely Ceased?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1934.
The Civil Disobedience Movement began with the famous Dandi March of Gandhi on 12 March 1930. The campaign was completely ceased in 1934.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): During the Quit India Movement of 1942, Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Indian flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai.
Reason (R): Sarojini Naidu was popularly called the 'Grand Old Lady of the Independence Movement.'
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.
  • Assertion (A) is true: During the Quit India Movement of 1942, Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Indian flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai.
  • Reason (R) is false: Aruna Asaf Ali (not Sarojini Naidu) was popularly known as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Independence Movement.

questions.question: Who among the following was the only martyr of the Quit India phase of the freedom movement who was hanged?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kushal Konwar.
Facts about the Quit India Movement:
  • The Quit India Resolution was passed by the Congress Working Committee on 8 August 1942 in Bombay
  • 'Quit India' or 'Bharat Chodo' slogan was given during this movement
  • Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or die'
  • It is also known as the August Movement or August Kranti
  • Kushal Konwar was the only martyr of the Quit India phase who was hanged

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding newspapers started by Mahatma Gandhi:
1. Indian Opinion was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa in 1903, along with M. H. Nazar.
2. Young India and Navajivan were newspapers later published by Gandhi after his return to India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.
  • Statement 1 is correct: Indian Opinion was established in 1903 in Durban, South Africa, by Mahatma Gandhi and M. H. Nazar.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Young India and Navajivan were newspapers published by Gandhi after his return to India.

questions.question: C Rajagopalakshari led the Salt Satyagraha in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.
The Salt March (Dandi Satyagraha, 12th March 1930 to 6th April 1930) was an act of nonviolent civil disobedience led by Mahatma Gandhi. C. Rajagopalachari led the Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu. Other leaders included K. Kelappan (Malabar) and Gopabandhu Chaudhary (Orissa).

questions.question:
Given below are the two columns. Column A consists of Events or terms and column B consist of correct descriptions. Match the column A with correct description in Column B
Column AColumn B
A. Anglo-Russian rivalry1. Opened Sindh's rivers and roads to British trade.
B. Subsidiary Treaty 18392. Forced on the Amirs of Sindh before annexation.
C. Sir Charles Napier3. Had commercial value, attracted British interest.
D. River Sindh4. Led military campaign to annex Sindh; called it a 'tassality'.
E. Treaty of 18325. Led Britain to expand influence in Afghanistan and Persia
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A-5, B-2, C-4, D-3, E-1.
  • Anglo-Russian rivalry (The Great Game) compelled Britain to expand its influence in Afghanistan and Persia to counter Russia (A-5).
  • The Subsidiary Treaty of 1839 was imposed on the Amirs of Sindh before annexation (B-2).
  • Sir Charles Napier led the campaign to annex Sindh and famously called it a 'tassality' (C-4).
  • The River Sindh held great commercial value, attracting British interest (D-3).
  • The Treaty of 1832 opened Sindh's rivers and roads to British trade (E-1).

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the broader geopolitical shift triggered by the decisive defeat of the Nawab of Carnatic's forces in their confrontation with European powers?
questions.option_1: It revealed systemic vulnerabilities in native military structures, prompting European companies to transition from trade to political hegemony.
questions.option_2: It disillusioned European companies, resulting in a strategic withdrawal from inland military affairs.
questions.option_3: It consolidated indigenous authority, forcing European traders into commercial treaties under local oversight.
questions.option_4: It established a stable dual administrative system between Indian principalities and foreign chartered companies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is It revealed systemic vulnerabilities in native military structures, prompting European companies to transition from trade to political hegemony.
The defeat of the Nawab of Carnatic's forces exposed the weakness of traditional Indian armies against the disciplined, technologically advanced European forces. This marked a turning point where European trading companies, especially the British, realized the possibility of extending political control beyond commerce. Gradually, their role shifted from merchants to power brokers in Indian politics. Thus, the Carnatic wars laid the foundation for European political dominance in India.

questions.question:
Assertion: The Treaty of Paris (1763) limited French settlements in India to trading posts only.
Reason: The French could no longer station troops or fortify their factories after the treaty.
questions.option_1: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended both the Seven Years' War and the Third Carnatic War, marking the British East India Company's decisive victory over the French in India. After the Battle of Wandiwash, France lost its political influence and was limited to trading in its enclaves. The French could no longer station troops or fortify their factories, which explains why their settlements were limited to trading posts only.

questions.question:
Assertion(A): Sir Charles Napier justified the annexation of Sindh on moral and legal grounds.
Reason(R): He described it as 'a useful humane piece of rascality.'
questions.option_1: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_3: A is false, but R is true.
questions.option_4: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is false, but R is true.
The annexation of Sindh (1843) was carried out by Sir Charles Napier after the Battle of Miani. Napier himself admitted that the conquest was not morally or legally justified. He cynically remarked on the annexation, calling it 'a useful humane piece of rascality', thereby acknowledging its dubious morality. Therefore, the assertion is false while the reason is true.
